issues.note: the fix belongs in js-sdk-toolchain: the local preview answers POST /content/entities/active for the wearable's parcel with [], and that entity id is the shared session key for both the LiveKit local scene room and the Pulse realm (lsd:<id>, a contract documented in js-sdk-toolchain docs/lsd-identity-and-pulse-realm.md); substituting another id on the Explorer side only works if sdk-commands keys its room on the same id, so the preview must return a scene-like entity for its pointers (sdk-commands start/server/endpoints.ts) or define a wearable-preview id in that contract

no category-specific code in the spring-bone path; the main suspect is that in-world compute skinning maps wearable bones to the avatar skeleton by list position (AttachmentAssetUtility.cs:128/151, ComputeSkinningBufferContainer.cs:92/129) while the Builder preview maps them by name, so a GLB that lists spring bones between avatar bones shifts the chain onto shoulder/arm bones; confirming needs the GLBs (only in Slack, not attached to the issue), and the real fix (bind by bone name when building skinning buffers) changes the GPU skinning path and needs on-device verification

the player's network, not the client or our backend: media.decentraland-dashboard.org (third-party, behind Cloudflare) resolves over IPv4 and IPv6 and serves the scene's .mp4/.jpg with 200/206 from here, the scene allowlists that host so the client's media gating passes, and Curl error 7 (TCP connect failure) also hits the scene's images on the same host, so it is not the AVPro/custom Windows video player; the user should check ISP, firewall or DNS access to Cloudflare
